heading: $ ls ~/projects
intro: Nine repositories from Vamsee's GitHub account, covering ML operations, forecasting, fraud detection, security and data engineering. Where a project is based on someone else's open-source work, its card credits the original author.

projects.name: driftguard
projects.title: driftguard
projects.summary: An end-to-end ML lifecycle that monitors itself: train, register in MLflow, serve with FastAPI, detect drift, retrain. It is demonstrated on 2011 to 2012 bike-share demand, a shift that feature-only monitoring would miss.
projects.result: Reported in the repo: held-out MAE down 44.6% after automatic retraining.
projects.imageAlt: Illustration of a drifting distribution above a loop of gauge, model and wrench

projects.name: surecast
projects.title: surecast
projects.summary: A day-ahead bike-share demand forecaster that reports its uncertainty. Conformalized quantile regression gives prediction intervals, SHAP explains each forecast, and rolling-origin backtests guard against leakage. Includes a Streamlit dashboard.
projects.result: Reported: gradient boosting MAE 42.7 against 55.7 for a seasonal baseline.
projects.imageAlt: Illustration of a forecast line with a widening shaded prediction interval

projects.name: creditcardfrauddetection-mlops
projects.title: Credit Card Fraud Detection
projects.summary: A Flask app for scoring card transactions. Pick logistic regression, random forest or XGBoost, enter a transaction, and get a fraud probability, a risk tier and a plain-language explanation from an LLM. Packaged with Docker.
projects.result: Three selectable models and low, medium and high risk tiers.
projects.imageAlt: Illustration of a credit card under a magnifying glass beside a shipping container and a dashboard

projects.name: modelcard
projects.title: modelcard
projects.summary: Generates a deterministic Markdown model card from a scikit-learn estimator and its metrics, as a library and a command-line tool. Identical inputs give byte-identical output, so cards can be diffed in CI.
projects.result: Runs fully offline; the demo uses scikit-learn's bundled Iris data.
projects.imageAlt: Illustration of a model feeding an arrow into a card with feature-importance bars

projects.name: fraud-detection-in-python
projects.title: Fraud Detection in Python
projects.summary: Compares fraud classifiers on 594,643 simulated bank transactions, 7,200 of them fraudulent: naive Bayes, logistic regression, a neural network, a decision tree and a random forest.
projects.credit: Originally developed for CSE 891 Data Mining at Michigan State University by Baylee Adams and Kyle Shope, per the repo README.
projects.imageAlt: Illustration of a decision tree with one leaf under a magnifying glass beside a stack of transaction slips

projects.name: text-analysis-using-nlp-streamlit
projects.title: Text Analysis with NLP
projects.summary: A Streamlit app for text preprocessing, sentiment analysis, named-entity recognition, part-of-speech tagging and word clouds.
projects.result: Parameters for each task can be adjusted in the interface.
projects.credit: Based on Text-Analysis-Using-NLP-Streamlit by Mohammadreza Mohammadi (MIT license).
projects.imageAlt: Illustration of a page with highlighted words, a sentiment bubble and a word cloud

projects.name: ai_soc
projects.title: AI-Augmented SOC
projects.summary: A research-grade, AI-assisted security operations centre. ML intrusion detection on CICIDS2017 features, LLM alert triage through Ollama, RAG over MITRE ATT&CK and CVE data, Wazuh ingestion and attack-campaign simulation.
projects.result: Local-first: alert triage runs on a local Ollama model, not a hosted API.
projects.credit: Based on AI_SOC by Abdul Bari (Apache-2.0 license).
projects.imageAlt: Illustration of a shield containing a network graph with one flagged node

projects.name: infohunter
projects.title: InfoHunter
projects.summary: A modular open-source-intelligence toolkit for usernames, emails and domains. It draws on sources such as Sherlock, Maigret, Holehe, HIBP, WHOIS and Shodan, and writes PDF or JSON reports.
projects.imageAlt: Illustration of a magnifying glass over a network of profile cards, a globe and an envelope

projects.name: goodreads_etl_pipeline
projects.title: Goodreads Data Pipeline
projects.summary: A batch pipeline for Goodreads data. A Python API wrapper lands files in S3, Spark jobs transform them, Redshift stores the results, and Airflow schedules runs and data-quality checks.
projects.result: Spark jobs are scheduled in Airflow to run every 10 minutes.
projects.credit: Based on goodreads_etl_pipeline by Sanchit Kumar (MIT license).
projects.imageAlt: Illustration of books flowing through cloud storage, a processing engine and a scheduler into a warehouse
